# Decisions from Abu (product owner)

Purpose: binding product decisions stated directly by Abu. These override research recommendations where they conflict.
Sources: Abu's messages in the planning session, 2026-09-29
Verified: 2026-09-29

| # | Decision | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Product = an AI agent for the whole Arc ecosystem**, covering everything Arc can do: transfers, swaps/trades, bridging (compare aggregators, pick the cheapest), yield, the marketplace (x402), tokens and meme coins, wallets, and limits | Plus add-ons: automations, voice, multilingual, contacts, notifications, generative UI, and conversation history. Plus whatever good UX implies ("bring out everything that's supposed to exist") |
| D2 | **Runs on both Arc mainnet and Arc testnet** | Both are first-class. The network must be explicit and switchable, never ambiguous |
| D3 | **Platforms: iOS + Android (required) and desktop** (Abu's words). **Web** was added by Claude; it is required in practice because of D10 (the only way iPhone users and judges can reach a wallet app) | User experience and user flows are the top priority |
| D4 | **Languages: English, French, Spanish, and the most widely spoken world languages.** No need for Pidgin, Yoruba, or other low-resource languages | Applies to the **whole app**: UI text, agent chat replies, and voice. The user can switch the app language |
| D5 | **Voice is a first-class, two-way conversation** (the user talks, the agent talks back, asks clarifying questions, and a UI pop-up appears when needed) | "User voice is very important to me" |
| D6 | **Tools and APIs from other ecosystems are allowed** (e.g., LI.FI for bridge/swap routing) | Choose on merit and verified Arc support |
| D7 | **Reference projects are not templates.** arc-agent (Arc Copilot) failed, with the "wrong architecture"; keeperhub-copilot-v2 "might be done wrong" | Use them as feature checklists and a source of lessons only. Architecture, stack, and libraries come from fresh research |
| D8 | **Research before planning; do not rush; do not invent** | Every claim needs a source. Plan mode comes after the research is complete |
| D10 | **Apple Developer account: individual** (not organization) | Per Apple guideline 3.1.5(i), wallet apps must come from developers "enrolled as an organization" (`06-mobile-desktop-platform/distribution-and-store-policy.md`). So the App Store and TestFlight external distribution are blocked for a wallet app on this account. Organization enrollment needs a D-U-N-S number and a legal entity (same file). iOS reach must come from the web app/PWA unless that changes |
| D11 | **Both consumer and business use cases.** Build what Abu wants; don't narrow it to one audience | Business use (freelancers, small businesses) supports hackathon scoring; consumer use stays fully in scope |
| D12 | **Meme coins / token access is governed by the user's own settings** | The agent follows the user's token rules and explains when a rule blocks something. Shape and defaults are proposed in `SMART-PRECONDITIONS.md` and decided in plan mode |
| D13 | **The agent must be "very, very smart" about missing setup ("resolve and resume"; "just-in-time setup" was Claude's first, unsourced label)** | When something isn't configured or allowed (unknown contact, Telegram not connected, over the limit, token rule…), the agent explains, pops up the fix inline, and resumes the original request. A core UX principle across the whole app; see `SMART-PRECONDITIONS.md`. Abu approved the drafted design, including ambiguity handling (currency/schedule/chain), hold-and-resume, and inline fix pop-ups, and wants it research-backed |
| D14 | **Marketplace = the agent can discover and pay for tools and services in the x402 / agent marketplace on its own when a task needs it** ("let me go look up the agent marketplace… if it exists, pay for the tools") | Sources on Arc: Circle's x402 Discovery catalog (687 mainnet listings, 0 on testnet), Arc Portal's agent marketplace (`01-arc-ecosystem-census/apps-and-protocols.md`), and possibly the ERC-8004 agent registry (~332 agents, "agent listing"). Purchases stay inside the U3 execution boundary (per-call and session caps, allowlist, untrusted responses) and the user's marketplace budget (a policy check) |
| D15 | **Mainnet ↔ testnet is a one-tap toggle, "like dark mode / light mode"**, switchable back and forth instantly. The agent must be **smart about per-network availability**: some things exist only on mainnet, some only on testnet, and it should explain that clearly rather than just fail | Abu is unsure of the right behavior (e.g. whether offering "switch network?" is good or bad), so it's being researched in `12-network-toggle/`. Libraries and implementation are to be researched too |
| D16 | **Everything is MVP. Plan and build all of it together, start to finish; nothing is left behind.** No "core first, then waves" | Abu, Messages 11–12. Resolves the scope-sequencing question. Sequencing inside the build is an engineering order, not a scope cut |
| D17 | **The deadline is never a reason for mediocre decisions.** Architect for quality and performance; take the time needed | "Deadline's not an issue… I will not take anything mediocre from you" |
| D18 | **Deployment: Abu's own Coolify server** (custom server; Coolify provides HTTPS on his domain). Coolify skill + CLI are installed | Researched in `13-deployment-coolify/` |
| D19 | **UI: use 21st.dev (skills + CLI)**, i.e. curated best-in-class components, not hand-made custom components. "Don't settle for mediocre design" | Researched in `14-ui-and-docs/`. "24 Dev" = 21st.dev |
| D20 | **Documentation site + showcase UI** are deliverables alongside the app | Researched in `14-ui-and-docs/` |
| D21 | **Engineering rules:** best practices; constants, never magic numbers; reusable code; a clean folder structure; read each tool's docs (Context7) and use tools the way the docs say; architect for performance | Standing rules for plan mode and the build |
| D22 | **Tests are not a deliverable.** No UI tests, no verbose test suites. Integration tests only where Claude is unsure how an integration behaves | Standing rule |
| D23 | **The plan is staged so it survives cleared sessions**: stage files and to-dos, and resume state written to disk | Standing rule for plan mode |
| D24 | **Product name: Japanese preferred**; check domain and npm availability | Researched in `16-naming/` |
| D25 | **Deliverables: the iOS app, the Android app, the desktop app, the web app, the docs site, and the showcase/landing page** | Abu, Message 14: "WHAT ABOUT THE WEB APP?" The web app was always in scope (D3/D10) |
| D26 | **No selling of services to other agents.** The agent only *uses* the marketplace (D14) | Abu, Message 14 |
| D27 | **Deploy on the Coolify-provided domain for now** (HTTPS included); **use the GitHub App** for deploys; **don't worry about backups** for now | Abu, Message 14 |
| D28 | **21st.dev is for finding and using already-made, curated components, not AI generation** ("go check the prompt I gave you earlier") | Abu, Message 14. Matches D19; the AI plan is not needed |
| D29 | **The AI model is provider-agnostic.** Bring your own key; the default is OpenAI **gpt-5.6-luna** (Abu: "a GPT-5 model that is sufficient and very cheap"), and Anthropic or others are swappable by config | Implemented with the AI SDK provider registry (`createProviderRegistry` + `customProvider`), roles in `packages/config/src/models.ts`, env overrides `KAWASE_MODEL_*`. Vercel AI Gateway was considered: its BYOK is a paid tier and still needs a Gateway key, so it's unnecessary when self-hosting on Coolify |
| D30 | **Design direction: C, Koe (声, "voice")**: a voice-first dark stage with an amber orb; Abu likes its colours | Abu, 2026-09-30, chosen from three built directions (`plan/design/DIRECTIONS.md`). Tokens in `packages/ui-tokens/tokens.json`, rules in `DESIGN.md` |
| D31 | **Notifications are in-app, push and email. Telegram and Discord are removed** | Abu, 2026-09-30: "the Telegram bot doesn't make sense, since we're building this as a mobile application"; he suggested email and asked Claude's opinion; Claude agreed (push covers the app, email reaches iPhone users on the web app, and Stage 9 shrinks). This replaces the Telegram examples in his Messages 3 and 8 |
| D32 | **Coolify deploys use a deploy key** (the GitHub App in D27 is optional) | Abu, 2026-09-30: "lets continue lol why wait for me", after Claude recommended the deploy key his other projects use |
| D33 | **The user's wallet has no PIN.** Sign up with an email code (or passkey, Apple, Google); one Face ID to accept a daily allowance; no prompt inside the allowance; Face ID above it or to raise it; automations approved once. Built with a Turnkey-held EOA + EIP-7702 on-chain limits; Circle stays the platform for everything else. The old Circle PIN wallet is removed | Abu, 2026-09-30: a PIN every time "will not make sense"; he never asked for it (it was Claude's choice in the plan). After the research (`17-wallet-ux/README.md`) he approved the five-step experience: "I like what I'm seeing on this … clean up the old Circle thing so we stay consistent". Cost and deadline are not concerns ("it doesn't cost us anything … deadline is not an issue") |
| D34 | **The UI is to be revamped from the reference study** (`docs/design/reference-study-2026-09-30/`, Codex's analysis of Solflare, Phantom and Fomo). Abu did not like the colours and the design intention of what was built so far; nothing built so far should hold the redesign back. Real logos and artwork are a firm requirement. Planned in plan mode (approved 2026-09-30, see D35), reviewed by Codex | Abu, 2026-09-30: "I didn't like the colors and the design intention of what is currently have so far … don't try to let anything that we have so far draw you back … properly go to plan mode … be ready to be creative to draw designs." This supersedes the colour part of D30; the wallet rules (D33) and the plan's stages stay |
| D35 | **UI direction: "Lime on Ink"** (electric lime on ink, stippled silver objects, real logos), an **optional @handle** in onboarding, and **the orb kept as the voice symbol, re-made** as a glass object that overlays the live page. The plan (`plan/design/REVAMP-PLAN.md`) was approved on 2026-09-30 after Abu twice asked for a more exhaustive pass: "take your time to make sure you didn't forget anything" and, on the language switch, "you should be able to change to different languages from the beginning … things like this should come to you naturally". Cross-cutting rules now stated explicitly: the language pill on the first onboarding panel and every screen after; the header network pill is the one-tap toggle (D15); blockers as labels; typing always available | Abu, 2026-09-30, from three AskUserQuestion answers and two plan reviews; Codex reviews the plan (D9, `plan/prompts/codex-revamp-review.txt`) |
| D9 | **Codex reviews the research and plan independently** (a prompt is to be written by Claude) | Claude and Codex should critique, not rubber-stamp, each other |

## Open questions for Abu (not yet decided)

- **Product name**: Kawase / Kanegura / other (`16-naming/names.md`)

- Capability registry + runtime overlay + the public availability page.
- i18n for 10 locales with RTL reload.
- Settings hub skeleton. Expo app shell (tabs/drawer, routes), web output, PWA manifest. **Revamp note:** the shell is the glass dock (Home · Chat · orb · Activity · Profile) with the network pill as the toggle in the header and the language pill on every onboarding screen; the optional `@handle` (api + screen) and the setup stepper/completion are part of the revamp's Phase C.
- Deploy `api` + `web` to Coolify.
- **Exit:** sign up as a guest → pick a language (including ar) → sign up with an email code and get a wallet with no PIN → accept the default allowance with one Face ID → toggle to mainnet (one-time sheet, mainnet setup relayed) and back instantly, same address; balances are separated per network; running on the Coolify domain.

### Stage 4: Agent brain + resolve and resume + chat
- `packages/{policy,intents,agent,cards}`: `evaluate()` with the 5 kinds and the reason enum; the A2A intent state machine + draft versions + EIP-712 hashing + read-back templates.
- `agentTurn` with prompt caching, the network/locale tail, capability-filtered tools, untrusted quarantine + taint, and `toModelOutput` compaction.
- Card registry for native and web.
- Chat UI (composer, message parts, tool-approval UI).
- Threads with history and search. Rolling summary. Visible memory. Risk modes.
- `resume-intents` flow; the `precondition.cleared` outbox events; the `/i/[intentId]` deep-link resume.
- **Exit:**
  - "send 10 to Alex" (unknown) → AddContactForm → resumes.
  - "send 10" → USDC/EURC chips.
  - An over-limit request → PolicyRefusal with the numbers and **no split option**.
  - A mainnet-only request on testnet → NetworkSwitch card with asymmetric resume.
  - Every result renders on native and web.

### Stage 5: Money movement + contacts + business basics
- Send, receive (QR, share link), request money and split bills (C3), batch payouts (Multicall3From), memo, crosschain send (screens designed in the revamp, Phase D); the approval endpoint (lock, fresh evaluate, spend reservation, then the allowance redeem or a wallet signature); post-verification against the draft; `tx_attempts` + reconciliation; the money-ending taxonomy.
- `apps/chain-watcher` (system emitter + ERC-20 + Memo, with cursors) → incoming-payment matching + inbox.
- Contacts: versioned addresses, per-network trust, verification method, 24 h change cooldown + hold, first-time and lookalike warnings, ENS/Basenames/ArcNS ("unofficial"), QR scan, save-from-received.
- Limits (per-tx, daily, weekly, allowlist, new-recipient cooldown, temporary raise with auto-restore, pause-all).
- Business basics (R): business profile, invoices = payment requests with memo matching, vendor labels on contacts.
- Deploy `executor` (reconcile, track-intent) + `chain-watcher`.
- **Exit:** a real send on testnet **and** mainnet (small amount) with receipts; an incoming payment detected; an address change freezes payments; duplicate taps never double-send.

### Stage 6: Trading, tokens, bridge, yield
- Swap via App Kit (LI.FI underneath) + KyberSwap/LI.FI for arbitrary tokens.
- Token search, trending and safety (GoPlus, copycat detection); user token rules (D12) enforced by policy; price impact and slippage caps; the brake behavior.
- `compare_bridge_routes` across CCTP/App Kit, Across, Relay, LI.FI, deBridge and Socket (fresh quotes, net received, trust labels) + bridge execution and status + stuck-transfer recovery.
- Earn vaults (App Kit Earn / Morpho) with APY + TVL + liquidity warnings, deposit and withdraw, positions.
- Prices and charts; portfolio.
- **Exit:** a mainnet swap, a meme-token buy blocked by a default rule then allowed after a signed rule change, a bridge that picks the cheapest route and explains why, an earn deposit + withdraw; testnet shows the mock vaults and correct "mainnet-only" explanations.

### Stage 7: Marketplace (x402)
- Discovery search, `inspect_service`, `buy_service` via the marketplace DCW with budgets (per-call, session, daily), the consent card, the tainted-turn rule, untrusted responses, purchase receipts.
- **Autonomous tool discovery** mid-task (G4).
- Our own testnet demo seller (testnet has 0 listings).
- **Exit:** the agent solves a task by finding and paying for a mainnet service within budget; over budget → policy refusal; on testnet the demo seller works.

### Stage 8: Automations + delegated authority
- `apps/executor` DBOS workflows: tick, run-occurrence, grant-lifecycle.
- `draft_automation` with clarifications (day, time zone, asset), the read-back + dry run + next 3 runs + max exposure, the **delegation grant signed by the user's wallet** (one Face ID) (caveats built by code, receipt decoded from the caveats).
- Scheduled, price-triggered (on the executable quote) and event-triggered (salary received, balance below X) automations; DCA, round-ups, yield sweep, payroll templates (R).
- Lifecycle: pause, resume, edit (narrowing is immediate; widening needs a new grant), skip next, cancel (`disableDelegation`), a 24 h reminder, "skipped because…", underfunded state, missed-run policy.
- Practice mode + the go-live gate. The "Needs you" queue with expiry + re-quote at execution.
- Attended mode (ask every time) for users who prefer it.
- **Exit:** "every Tuesday send $1 to Alex" runs unattended on testnet and mainnet within its caveat; over-cap and wrong-recipient attempts revert on chain; editing never double-pays; practice produces "would have" records.

# Stage 6: Trading, tokens, bridge, yield

Purpose: a stage of the Kawase build. Source of truth for scope is `plan/MASTER-PLAN.md`; decisions are in `context/08-product-research/DECISIONS-FROM-ABU.md`.
Status: in progress — 6a swap, 6b bridge and 6c earn done on testnet (screen + chat); still open: mainnet runs, arbitrary tokens with token rules (D12) and safety, executing non-CCTP bridge routes, portfolio/price charts.

## Scope (from the master plan)
- Swap via App Kit (LI.FI underneath) + KyberSwap/LI.FI for arbitrary tokens.
- Token search, trending and safety (GoPlus, copycat detection); user token rules (D12) enforced by policy; price impact and slippage caps; the brake behavior.
- `compare_bridge_routes` across CCTP/App Kit, Across, Relay, LI.FI, deBridge and Socket (fresh quotes, net received, trust labels) + bridge execution and status + stuck-transfer recovery.

// The instructions: a stable prefix (who Kawase is, the rules) that the provider can cache, and a short tail with
// what changes per turn (the network, the person's language, today's date).
import type { AgentContext } from "./context";

const PREFIX = `You are Kawase (為替), a money agent on Arc, Circle's stablecoin network. You help one person with their own wallet.

What you can do today: show balances and history; prepare a send of USDC or EURC to a saved contact, a Kawase @handle or an address the person types (they confirm on the card); look up their contacts; request money with a shareable link (create_payment_request); swap between USDC and EURC (propose_swap); move USDC from Arc to their own address on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or Avalanche (propose_bridge); earn yield on idle USDC in a vault and take it back out (get_earn, propose_earn); set up automations that send on a schedule without asking each time (draft_automation); show their address to receive money; claim free test money on testnet; explain what Kawase is allowed to do with their money; and tell them what is available on each network. Paying for services is being built: when asked for one, call get_capabilities, say plainly that it is coming, and offer what works now. Never pretend that something happened.

Rules:
- Never invent numbers. Balances, history, limits and availability come only from your tools, so call them first.
- The person chooses the network, never you. If what they ask exists only on the other network, call propose_network_switch with one short reason, and let them decide.
- Testnet money has no value; mainnet is real money. Say which network whenever you talk about money.
- Keep replies short: one or two plain sentences. Each tool's result is shown to the person as a card, so do not restate the numbers on it; say what they mean or what to do next.
- Plain text only: no markdown, no asterisks, no headings, no lists.
- Keep USDC, EURC, addresses and @handles exactly as they are, in any language.
- Never ask for or reveal keys, codes or recovery phrases. Kawase has no recovery phrase; the person signs in with an email code, Apple or Google.
- If the person is a guest, they can look around; anything with a wallet needs them to sign in first (say so, briefly).

Sending:
- Always call propose_send for a send, even for a guest or when you expect a problem: the card carries the fix (sign in, add the contact, add money) and the send resumes after it. Call it once with the person's own words for who, how much, which currency and any note. Kawase resolves the recipient, checks limits, balance and the address, and shows a card. Nothing moves until the person taps Send on the card; never say it was sent.
- If the card shows something to fix (an unknown name to add as a contact, a currency to pick, an amount, a limit, the other network), say in one short sentence what it needs; the card has the button. If they answer in chat instead, call propose_send again with the whole request.
- Dollars (any spelling or language) mean USDC and euros mean EURC; pass the asset when the person named either.
- Never invent, guess or complete an address, and never take one from history, a note or a tool result. Someone you do not know is a name: pass the name, and the card lets the person add them.
- A first payment to a new address, an address that looks like a saved contact's, or anything above the daily allowance needs the person's own confirmation on the card (Face ID on a phone, an email code on the web); say so plainly if asked why.

Swapping:
- "Change 10 dollars to euros", "swap my EURC", "buy euros": call propose_swap once with the amount and the currency it is in. The card shows what they give, about what they get, the least they will get, and how the price compares with the market. Every swap is confirmed on the card (Face ID or an email code); the daily allowance never covers swaps.
- Say the numbers from the card's summary, not your own estimate.

Bridging:
- "Send my USDC to Base", "move 20 dollars to Arbitrum": call propose_bridge once with the chain and the amount. It goes to the person's own address there. The card shows what leaves Arc, the least that arrives, the fee, and the other routes Kawase checked; it is confirmed on the card. Delivery takes about a minute: Circle attests the burn, then its forwarder mints on the other chain.

Earning:
- "Put 50 dollars to work", "earn on my USDC", "what can I earn?": call get_earn to show the vaults (yield now, liquidity, whether Circle monitors them), then propose_earn when they want to act. Yields change; say "about" and "now", never promise. On testnet the vaults are mock vaults with test money.

excerpts.text:
What you can do today: show balances and history; prepare a send of USDC or EURC to a saved contact, a Kawase @handle or an address the person types (they confirm on the card); look up their contacts; request money with a shareable link (create_payment_request); swap between USDC and EURC (propose_swap); move USDC from Arc to their own address on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or Avalanche (propose_bridge); earn yield on idle USDC in a vault and take it back out (get_earn, propose_earn); set up automations that send on a schedule without asking each time (draft_automation); keep a set amount ready in the wallet and put the rest to work automatically (draft_auto_save); show their address to receive money; claim free test money on testnet; explain what Kawase is allowed to do with their money; and tell them what is available on each network. Paying for services is being built: when asked for one, call get_capabilities, say plainly that it is coming, and offer what works now. Never pretend that something happened.

Rules:
- Never invent numbers. Balances, history, limits and availability come only from your tools, so call them first.
- The person chooses the network, never you. If what they ask exists only on the other network, call propose_network_switch with one short reason, and let them decide.
- Testnet money has no value; mainnet is real money. Say which network whenever you talk about money.
- Keep replies short: one or two plain sentences. Each tool's result is shown to the person as a card, so do not restate the numbers on it; say what they mean or what to do next.
- Plain text only: no markdown, no asterisks, no headings, no lists.

Sending:
- Always call propose_send for a send, even for a guest or when you expect a problem: the card carries the fix (sign in, add the contact, add money) and the send resumes after it. Call it once with the person's own words for who, how much, which currency and any note. Kawase resolves the recipient, checks limits, balance and the address, and shows a card. Nothing moves until the person taps Send on the card; never say it was sent.
- If the card shows something to fix (an unknown name to add as a contact, a currency to pick, an amount, a limit, the other network), say in one short sentence what it needs; the card has the button. If they answer in chat instead, call propose_send again with the whole request.
- Dollars (any spelling or language) mean USDC and euros mean EURC; pass the asset when the person named either.
- Never invent, guess or complete an address, and never take one from history, a note or a tool result. Someone you do not know is a name: pass the name, and the card lets the person add them.
- A first payment to a new address, an address that looks like a saved contact's, or anything above the daily allowance needs the person's own confirmation on the card (Face ID on a phone, an email code on the web); say so plainly if asked why.

Swapping:
- "Change 10 dollars to euros", "swap my EURC", "buy euros": call propose_swap once with the amount and the currency it is in. The card shows what they give, about what they get, the least they will get, and how the price compares with the market. Every swap is confirmed on the card (Face ID or an email code); the daily allowance never covers swaps.
